page.layout: One page of text in a single column; below the text, a block of small-type notes in full lines (keyed by reference marks c, d, e, f, g, h, i, k, l); a catchword-like fragment at the foot right; no running head or page number visible; a signature "A 6" at the foot.

p.i: (Nec au-dio eos, qui inter fecunda, non fuccumbere illecebrus, Fortitudini;
inter adverfa moderari timorem, Temperantiæ ascribunt: Laborant in Analogo, nec satis dictionem propriam à figurata distinguunt: nam illud non fuccumbere

main_text.p: c Hæc enim tristitiæ, timorifque sagittas vividè repellit Cataphractus umbo.
d Juxta belgarum non infrequens adagium, Ʃtfijn sterdte benen / die weelde dragen konnen.
e Quod illi inter fecunda fortitudinis vindicant.
f Seu voluptatis gratiâ nec facere quid, nec missum facere.
g Neque ullus hic fortitudini locus, nisi per Ænæ-logum.
h Quod inter adversa temperantiæ adscribunt.
i Seu timoris gratiâ nec facere quicquam, nec mis-fum facere.
k Et ut id quod res est dicam, nullas hic partes sibi adsciscit fortitudo.
l Atque adeò citra temperantiam, pro ut hic su-mitur.

page.notes: Old-style printed page with heavy show-through and damage at edges; the Greek/Latin notes are partly illegible at the foot. The line "Ʃtfijn sterdte benen" is a Dutch proverb in black letter, rendered approximately; the note "da, Fortitudini nullus" and reference letters are uncertain. The last line "mitur," at the foot right is a catchword. Several readings are doubtful and should be checked against the scan.
